statement: Recent-graduate unemployment minus the all-worker rate >= 2.0 pp in any 2027 quarter (NY Fed College Labor Market, 2027 quarterly)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2024 (resolution window is 2027). The last in-phase update (Nov 2024, data to Sept 2024) put recent-graduate (22-27) unemployment at 5.3%, a ~3-year high, vs roughly 4.1-4.2% for all workers: a gap of ~1.1-1.2 pp, already unusually positive by historical standards (recent graduates were normally below the all-worker rate). Gap vs all college graduates was 2.8 pp, the widest since 1990 outside early pandemic months. Q1-Q2 2024 in-phase vintages not retrieved this run.

items.summary: Regional central bank's Q3 2024 update: recent-graduate unemployment 5.3% (Sept 2024, 3-month average), the highest in about three years. Labour market otherwise solid.
items.detail: NY Fed 'Labor Market for Recent College Graduates', 2024:Q3 update published Tuesday 2024-11-19, per Bloomberg / Employee Benefit News (2024-11-19) and Marketplace (2024-11-20, quoting NY Fed economist Richard Deitz). Verified via search snippets.

items.summary: Implied indicator gap at Sept 2024: ~1.3 pp (5.3% recent graduates vs ~4.0% all workers, NY Fed series), below the 2.0 pp threshold but positive and widening relative to 2022-23.
items.detail: NY Fed college labour market data (CSV, Wayback 2024-11-21): 2024-09 all workers 3.985%, recent graduates 5.303%. Gap computed by us; not a published NY Fed figure.

items.summary: In-phase vintages for Q4 2023-Q2 2024 updates were not retrieved; later-vintage annual averages (2024: 4.8% vs 3.9%) are excluded under the as-of rule. Bloc B publishes urban youth (16-24) unemployment but no comparable recent-graduate vs all-worker series.
items.detail: The NY Fed CSV is revised with each update; archived 2024 vintages would be needed. Bloc B NBS youth rate (new method from Jan 2024, excl. students) not comparable.
